title: Shackled to the Machine: A DeepSeek-R1-8B Record on Four Raspberry Pi 5
description:
We evaluate CPU-only distributed inference of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B (dense 8B, Q40) on a four-node Raspberry Pi 5 (16 GB) cluster running distributed-llama. A clean-room measurement at the optimal thread count sustains 8.32 tok/s decode (n=20, 95% CI [8.30, 8.34]), bit-exact — to our knowledge the best published figure for this model on Raspberry Pi 5, 29% above the prior four-node record (6.43 tok/s) and 37% above the Seeed Studio configuration (6.06 tok/s). Decode throughput is shown to fall roughly linearly with context length as the KV-cache grows (the 8.32 figure is the short-context peak).

We attribute the gain by layer: the production binary is byte-identical to clean upstream, so the source/kernel changes contribute approximately zero to dense decode (they add 86% to prefill and 15.2% to a 30B Mixture-of-Experts model in the companion report). Dense decode is bound by memory bandwidth; the gains live in the hardware and operating-system layers, not the application kernels. We frame inference optimisation as a three-layer stack (hardware/firmware, operating system, application software): profile the binding constraint, then tune the layer it lives in. We additionally describe a bit-exact, adaptive prompt-lookup speculative decoder and a controlled dense-vs-MoE contrast on identical silicon. All figures are bit-exact (SHA-256 of the generated token-id stream at temperature 0, seed 42); no overclocking, quantisation change, or model substitution is used. Raw benchmark data and LaTeX sources are included.
